summary.text: Chris Deluzio is the Democratic incumbent for Pennsylvania's 17th District, first elected in 2022. A Pittsburgh-area native and Naval Academy graduate, he served as a Navy officer, including a deployment in Iraq, and then worked as a voting-rights and election-security attorney and policy director at Pitt Cyber. He serves on the Armed Services and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

paragraphs.text: Born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, in 1984; according to his official biography, he is a native of Thornburg and attended Bishop Canevin High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the United States Naval Academy in 2006 and a law degree from Georgetown University in 2013; his official biography says the law degree was awarded magna cum laude.
Commissioned as an active-duty surface warfare officer in the U.S. Navy; his service included three deployments, including a tour with U.S. Army Civil Affairs in Iraq.
After law school, clerked for a federal judge (Ballotpedia lists the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York) and worked in private legal practice.

Worked on the Voting Rights and Election Security teams at the Brennan Center for Justice, then as policy director of the University of Pittsburgh Institute for Cyber Law, Policy, and Security (Pitt Cyber).
Was part of the Pitt Faculty Organizing Committee with the United Steelworkers, which won a faculty union at the University of Pittsburgh.

First elected to Congress in 2022, defeating Sean Meloy in the May Democratic primary and Republican Jeremy Shaffer in the November general election; he was re-elected in 2024 over Republican Rob Mercuri.

Serves on the House Armed Services Committee (Readiness and Seapower and Projection Forces subcommittees) and the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee (Aviation and Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials subcommittees); he previously served on the House Veterans' Affairs Committee.
His official biography says he lives with his family in Allegheny County.
